claims.text: The author asked for a small, focused agent behaviour policy about tokens, in observe mode first: show the user what the session reads, caches, writes and costs, in a box under each answer.
claims.quote: Observe first: show the user what the session reads, caches, writes and costs.

claims.text: Every model call re-sends the system prompt, the tool definitions and the whole conversation, and the only thing that makes that affordable is the prompt cache.
claims.quote: the only thing that makes that affordable is the prompt cache

claims.text: Anthropic's Claude Code team runs alerts on its prompt cache hit rate and declares SEVs if they are too low, because a few points of cache miss rate dramatically affect cost and latency.
claims.quote: we run alerts on our prompt cache hit rate and declare SEVs if they're too low

claims.text: Asked by a system prompt to report its own usage, the model said twice, correctly, that it could not see the numbers; they existed, 37,019 tokens of input in the first turn, $0.05 and then $0.09, but nowhere it could read.
claims.quote: 37,019 tokens of input in the first turn, $0.05 and then $0.09

value.unit: input tokens in the first turn of the prompt test

claims.text: With the tokens hook the model reported a context of 37,087 tokens, 353 output tokens and about $0.05, exactly the first turn's figures, one turn behind because a hook that runs before the answer cannot count it.
claims.quote: They are one turn behind, because a hook that runs before the answer cannot count it.

claims.text: A prompt can ask for behaviour; only a hook can supply data, which is why hooks are the sweet spot for anything that has to be true rather than hoped for.
claims.quote: A prompt can ask for behaviour; only a hook can supply data

claims.text: No Claude Code hook event carries token usage in general; the only token fields are on a resumed or forked session's start, so everything else must come from the transcript, a JSON file with one line per event.
claims.quote: No event carries token usage in general

claims.text: Each response is written to the transcript several times, each line repeating the full usage: 2,621 lines carried usage for 1,165 responses, and 849 responses appeared more than once with identical figures.
claims.quote: 2,621 lines carried usage, for 1,165 responses; 849 responses appeared more than once, always with identical figures

value.unit: transcript lines carrying usage, for 1,165 responses

claims.text: Counting lines gave 1.06 billion cache-read tokens and counting responses gave 459 million; the site's own status report had been counting lines since it was written.
claims.quote: Counting lines gave 1.06 billion cache-read tokens; counting responses gave 459 million.

value.unit: cache-read tokens counted by response, against the line count

claims.text: The session's status report, which had said 2.9M out and 1.0B cached when the truth was 1.1 million and 460 million, now counts each message id once.
claims.quote: It now counts each message id once.

claims.text: In Claude Code 2.1.300 the transcript carries the request, not only the conversation: prompt_snapshot records hold the system prompt in 13 parts and all 49 tool definitions, about 34,000 and 198,000 characters, though the documentation does not say so.
claims.quote: the system prompt, in 13 parts, and all 49 tool definitions, about 34,000 and 198,000 characters

value.unit: tool definitions in the transcript's prompt snapshot

claims.text: At about four characters a token, the tool definitions alone are around 50,000 tokens, six times the system prompt, so a token hook can see the fixed cost of every call.
claims.quote: the tool definitions alone are around 50,000 tokens, six times the system prompt

value.unit: tokens of tool definitions per call, estimated

claims.text: Anything that can read the transcript can read everything the model was told, so a token hook should handle numbers only and never send text anywhere; the format is undocumented and may change.
claims.quote: a token hook should handle numbers only and never send text anywhere

claims.text: The hook is one Python file of 132 lines and a policy file; each run seeks to where it stopped, reads only the new lines, counts each response once, prices it by model and saves the totals.
claims.quote: The hook is one Python file of 132 lines and a policy file.

value.unit: lines of Python in the hook

claims.text: The first run on the session's 66 MB transcript took 252 milliseconds; every run after it took about one millisecond inside the hook and about 31 milliseconds including starting Python.
claims.quote: every run after it took about one millisecond inside the hook, and about 31 milliseconds including starting Python

value.unit: millisecond per warm run inside the hook

claims.text: The policy carries the version, the mode, the limits and the prices with their source, and the modes are observe, which shows and logs, warn, and enforce, which blocks the next prompt once the session's budget is spent.
claims.quote: observe shows and logs; warn also warns when a limit is crossed; enforce blocks the next prompt once the session's budget is spent

claims.text: Where the output goes decides who sees it: a systemMessage on Stop is shown to the user, additional context on UserPromptSubmit goes to the model so it can be frugal, and a log line stays on the machine.
claims.quote: Where the output goes decides who sees it.

claims.text: This session read 99% of its input from the cache: about $171.68 at policy prices, and reading the 467 million cached tokens fresh would have cost about $1,780 more.
claims.quote: reading those 467 million tokens fresh instead of from the cache would have cost about $1,780 more

value.unit: percent of input read from the cache in this session

claims.text: Claude Code already shows a lot without a hook: the status line, /usage and /context, and for a team the OpenTelemetry export sends a token usage metric and an event per API request, the central collector already built.
claims.quote: That is the central telemetry collector, already built.

claims.text: The hook still earns its place because it is a policy: it carries limits and modes, can tell the model, can block, and is the same small file wherever it runs; it can also send numbers to an sgit append lane.
claims.quote: it carries limits and modes, it can tell the model, it can block, and it is the same small file wherever it runs

claims.text: Sending to the append lane took the hook from about 31 to about 96 milliseconds a call, and all 20 test events arrived with nine fields each and no text.
claims.quote: all 20 test events arrived, with nine fields each and no text

value.unit: test events delivered to the append lane

claims.text: The coding agents are converging: Codex CLI has hooks, a /status command and OpenTelemetry; Gemini CLI has hooks around each model call and /stats; Cursor added hooks in version 1.7 on 29 September 2025.
claims.quote: The coding agents are converging on the same shape.

claims.text: GitHub Copilot moved to usage-based billing on 1 June 2026, Cline shows every token count and cost per task, and the chat apps show least: no token count per conversation was found in Claude.ai or ChatGPT.
claims.quote: I found no token count per conversation in Claude.ai or ChatGPT

claims.text: Caching differs by provider, OpenAI's on by default with discounts up to 95% and Gemini's implicit caching on by default, so the policy file is where the differences belong: one hook, one price table per provider.
claims.quote: one hook, one price table per provider

claims.text: tokens.hook.sgit.ai is proposed as the example of how a mission-critical hook should be run: a small code base, mapped completely as a graph, measured, tested on real transcripts and released like any other software.
claims.quote: a small code base, mapped completely, measured, and released like any other software

claims.text: Install and distribute: a few lines of settings for one user, managed settings or a plugin for an organisation, and for sgit users a vault with the hook, its policy and its releases, with an append lane beside it.
claims.quote: for sgit users, a vault with the hook, its policy and its releases, and an append lane beside it

claims.text: One tool, one version: the hook ran in Claude Code 2.1.300, and the transcript format is internal and may change.
claims.quote: The hook ran in Claude Code 2.1.300; the transcript format is internal and may change.

claims.text: The prompt test was small: two turns each, one model; other models may guess where this one refused.
claims.quote: Two turns each, one model; other models may guess where this one refused.

claims.text: Costs are at list prices; subscriptions, discounts and regional pricing change the bill.
claims.quote: Subscriptions, discounts and regional pricing change the bill.

claims.text: The token estimate for tool definitions is rough: characters divided by four.
claims.quote: The token estimate for tool definitions is rough. Characters divided by four.

claims.text: The other tools are described from their documentation, not run for this article.
claims.quote: The other tools are from their documentation. Not run for this article.

claims.text: tokens.hook.sgit.ai does not exist yet; it is the proposal.
claims.quote: tokens.hook.sgit.ai does not exist yet. It is the proposal.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo on 15 October 2026; the hook, experiments and measurements were made by the site's agent the same day, two research agents read the documentation, and the quotes were checked.
claims.quote: two research agents read the documentation, and the quotes were checked
